items.t: Why Did Colgate-Palmolive (CL) Shares Drop After Its Latest Update?
sum: Fresh earnings are driving the conversation around Colgate-Palmolive (CL) after the consumer products group reported third quarter 2026 results and lifted its full year outlook for sales and profitability.

Colgate-Palmolive's recent Q3 beat and higher full year guidance come after a strong run, with the share price delivering a 24.29% year to date return and a 25.54% total shareholder return over the past year, even though the stock slipped 2.16% on the day after the results.
See how Colgate-Palmolive compares to other consumer staples showing resilient earnings momentum by running the hand picked 29 resilient stocks with low risk scores alongside this latest Q3 update.

After Colgate-Palmolive's strong run and modest pullback, the share price now sits between its recent high, analyst targets and intrinsic estimates. Where does fair value really land within that range?

Colgate-Palmolive closed at $96.56, while the most followed narrative, according to rcb9, points to a fair value of $86.48 using a 7% discount rate. That gap frames the latest Q3 beat as impressive on execution but tight on valuation headroom.

A note on the shape of this result. Twenty four times forward Base Business earnings of roughly $3.88 implies about $93 today. This model returns $86.48. The whole difference is structural. When the discount rate exceeds the growth rate, five years at a three point gap costs about 16%. For a slow compounder this method is inherently more conservative than a simple multiple, and that is worth knowing before treating the output as a verdict rather than as one lens.
Still, this fair value lens could crack if North America stays weak for longer or if another impairment in skin health hits Colgate-Palmolive earnings quality.

Colgate Palmolive (CL) Stock Still Looks Reasonable Following Its 38% Five Year Run
sum: Colgate-Palmolive has turned in solid multi-year gains and a fresh run in 2026, so the real question now is whether the cash the business can produce over time lines up with the current share price. With the stock recently around US$95, investors are asking if the underlying cash flows support that level or if expectations have started to stretch.
Over the past 5 years, Colgate-Palmolive has returned about 38.0%, which puts real weight on whether that share price climb is matched by its long run cash generation potential.

Recent earnings strength, higher margin guidance and increased spending on premium products and advertising may support expectations for steadier cash flow and influence how investors think about the value of those future streams today.
The issue now is whether Colgate-Palmolive's current market value is justified by the intrinsic value suggested by its Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) estimate based on those cash flows.

If you are weighing Colgate-Palmolive against other options where valuation hinges on cash generation, a focused screen of 35 high quality undervalued stocks can provide another structured starting point for research.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach here weighs the cash Colgate-Palmolive is expected to generate for shareholders against the current price of US$95.62. Latest twelve-month free cash flow sits at about US$3.77b, and the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity model assumes that these owner earnings continue to grow rather than shrink over the coming decade.

In the model, projected free cash flows rise gradually and then settle into slower expansion in the later years, which aligns more closely with a mature global consumer products group rather than a high-growth story. Because the DCF projections put Colgate-Palmolive's estimated intrinsic value meaningfully above the current share price, the stock screens as undervalued on this cash flow lens. The Q3 2026 earnings beat, along with higher full-year guidance and firmer margin targets, helps explain why the model supports more value than the present market price embeds. How Investors May Respond To Colgate Stock After Raised Earnings Guidance
sum: Colgate-Palmolive reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$5,369 million and net income of US$751 million, then raised full year 2026 guidance with expected net sales growth of 4% to 5%, higher gross profit margin on a GAAP basis and double digit earnings per share growth.

The updated outlook pairs tighter cost discipline with increased advertising spend as a share of net sales, which suggests management is leaning on brand support rather than pulling back on growth investment to protect profitability.
Attention now turns to how Colgate-Palmolive's higher 2026 earnings guidance, including a stronger gross margin outlook, could reshape the longer term investment narrative.
See how Colgate-Palmolive's tighter cost control and higher earnings outlook compare with other branded consumer stocks by checking our hand-picked 33 high quality undervalued stocks.

To hold Colgate-Palmolive, you need to believe the premium oral care, emerging market exposure and Hill’s Pet Nutrition portfolio can keep earnings growing even when categories slow. The raised 2026 outlook points to better gross margin and disciplined costs, which supports that earnings story rather than reinventing it.

In the short term, the key swing factor is whether North America and pet food categories stabilize while higher advertising spend actually converts into volume and mix. The biggest risk still sits in weak demand in core markets and the recyclability class action, and the latest guidance update does not materially change those pressure points.

The most relevant fresh data point is the Q3 2026 result that sat behind the guidance lift. Colgate-Palmolive reported US$5,369 million in quarterly sales and US$751 million in net income, alongside basic EPS of US$0.94. Those figures, plus nine month numbers, gave management enough confidence to tighten full year expectations.

Is Procter & Gamble Stock Priced Right Against Its Peers?
sum: Procter & Gamble (PG) operates with a wider operating margin than its four rivals in household and personal care: Colgate-Palmolive, Church & Dwight, Estee Lauder and Kenvue. Over the past year, however, P&G stock returned the least of the five. Investors currently pay less for its earnings than they do for Church & Dwight’s. So how much less are you paying, and for how much more profit?

P&G stock currently trades at 22.2 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 31.8 times for Church & Dwight. Profitability metrics highlight a different balance. P&G had an operating margin of 22.7% over the same period, well above the 17.5% recorded for Church & Dwight. The two companies belong to different industry classifications, so what each sells may account for part of that margin gap. P&G also delivered faster top-line expansion, with revenue up 3.3% against 2.7% for Church & Dwight.

Colgate-Palmolive and Estee Lauder each recorded a loss in at least one of the past four quarters, so their P/Es do not provide a direct comparison with P&G’s. Among the peers, only Kenvue carries a lower P/E at 20.6 times earnings, and that company saw its revenue grow more slowly at 1.8%.
P&G is keeping a smaller portion of its sales as profit. The company posted an operating margin of 24% a year earlier, compared with 22.7% over the past twelve months.

In the latest quarter, revenue grew 1.5% from a year earlier. Management noted that market growth across North America and its main European markets has slowed by 1 to 2 points over the past 12 to 18 months.

Management is currently betting on better products to restart growth. Tide Original Liquid went from declining sales to high-single-digit growth after P&G improved the detergent without raising the price. Tide Evo, a new formula that P&G has patented, is set to roll out nationally in fiscal 2027.

Management expects organic sales to grow 1% to 3% in fiscal 2027, matching the expansion range it anticipates for its markets. Executives forecast core earnings per share of $6.89 to $7.11, compared with $6.89 in fiscal 2026. Hitting the low end of that guidance means no growth at all.
